title: Product law of special bits
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $p$ be a deterministic protocol on pairs of subsets of an $n$-element coordinate set, and let $z$ be an achievable value of the summary consisting of the transcript, special coordinate, Alice’s bits strictly before it, and Bob’s bits strictly after it. Under the uniform hard-sample law conditioned on the fiber with summary $z$, the law of the pair of special-coordinate bits is the product of the marginal law of Alice’s bit and the marginal law of Bob’s bit.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a deterministic protocol on pairs of subsets of an $n$-element coordinate set
replaced:
Fix a deterministic communication protocol $p$ for the disjointness problem on $n$
coordinates and an achievable value $z$ of the summary variable $Z = (M, T, X_{<T},
Y_{>T})$, whose components are the transcript $M$, the special coordinate $T$, the
vector $X_{<T}$ of Alice's bits at coordinates below $T$, and the vector $Y_{>T}$ of
Bob's bits at coordinates above $T$. Let $\nu$ be the uniform distribution on hard
samples conditioned on the fiber $\{Z = z\}$, let $\mu$ be the law of the special
bit-pair $(X_T, Y_T)$ under $\nu$, and let $\mu_X$ and $\mu_Y$ be the laws of the single
bits $X_T$ and $Y_T$ under $\nu$. Then
\[
\mu = \mu_X \otimes \mu_Y.
\]
